title: Planning an entry
next: Next: from the chart to your signals
outro_say: That's planning an entry. | It's a calculator: nothing is placed, and it's not advice.

steps.screen: A card: don't buy all at once
steps.say: Many traders don't buy all at once. | They place a ladder of orders below the price, so a dip fills them at better prices.

steps.screen: The ladder helper under the chart
steps.say: The ladder helper sits right under the chart. | Here, Bitcoin on one-hour candles.

steps.screen: Long or short, consolidating or trending
steps.say: Choose long or short, and the kind of market. | Consolidating gives equal orders close to the price. | Trending makes the nearest order smallest and the furthest largest.

steps.screen: Orders spaced by the daily move
steps.say: The orders are spaced by this coin's typical daily move, so a quiet coin gets a tight ladder and a wild one a wide ladder. | The stop sits beyond the last order.
Switch on Show on chart. | Blue lines for the orders, thicker for a bigger share, red for the stop, and grey for your average price if every order fills.

Or put the orders on Fibonacci levels. | It measures the last swing, or uses your own Fibonacci drawing, and the stop goes just past the swing. | Drawn on the same move, the Fibonacci lines meet the orders.
For the final entry, switch to five-minute candles. | They cover the last seven days, for crypto.
Switch the lines off when you're done.
